notes: Customer context: national transit operator; high-availability for rider-facing chat and ETA reranking; outages directly impact operations
Scale: peak concurrent requests estimated 12k QPS at regional level during rush windows, baseline 2-3k QPS off-peak
Primary ask: Dedicated GPU pools across 3 regions (na-east, na-west, eu-west) with active failover and 20-30% headroom for spikes
Latency targets: p50 <30ms, p95 <80-100ms for chat generation (end-to-end); embeddings p95 <60ms
Throughput guarantee: 10k tokens/sec sustained per region (reserved), burst to 40k tokens/sec (shared burst) during incident windows
Customer prefers pinning model families (llama-variant and a faster distilled model) and automatic fallback to smaller model on overload
Security notes: must support SAML SSO, KMS key ownership, audit logs retention 1 year, and optional on-prem enclave for PII flows
Quoted: 'We need deterministic throughput in rush hour — can't have noisy neighbor impact' (VP Infra)
Cost sensitivity: moderate-high; interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization to reduce reserved GPU count
POC asks: 4-week pilot with reserved pool in na-east and na-west, run synthetic rush-hour replay, failure injection for AZ loss, measure failover latency
reserved_gpu_plan: Plan A (recommended): na-east: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (2 AZs, 12 each), na-west: 16x reserved (2 AZs), eu-west: 12x reserved
Headroom: baseline reserve + 25% warm headroom for autoscaling slots and pre-warmed KV caches
Burst: additional shared burst pool (non-reserved) to be used with agreed backpressure and priority routing
Model placement: latency-sensitive small models colocated in same AZ as edge proxies; large-model shards distributed across AZs for redundancy
failover_strategy: Active-active across regions for read requests; write-heavy workflows route to primary with cross-region fallback
AZ failover: hot-standby capacity (>=50% of AZ reserved) to recover within 30s for token generation state and KV cache warming
Regional failover: pre-warmed caches and transparent model-variant fallback (distilled model) to meet latency SLOs during capacity constraint
Operational runbook: automated routing switch + alerting; manual escalation path to Redwood SRE for sustained cross-region incidents
poc_milestones: Week 0: Confirm traffic replay dataset and security binding (SAML test account + KMS key)
Week 1: Deploy dedicated pool in na-east and na-west; baseline perf run

Week 3: Quantization experiment + Redwood Optimize suggestions to reduce GPU count while meeting SLOs
Week 4: Final report, SLA draft, and recommended reserved capacity for year-1
